extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants / senior and key personnel preparing biosketch and Facilities & Other Resources
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing the NIH Biographical Sketch (senior/key personnel) and the Facilities & Other Resources section of an NIH grant application, including required fields, attachments, and descriptions of lab space, equipment, computing, and shared resources. Focuses on what to provide and the format/contents for each section.

rubrics_metrics.name: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH format / length
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified format exactly for each person and keep the biosketch within five pages; include the sections A–D (Personal Statement, Positions and Honors, Contributions to Science, Additional Information: Research Support).

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A personal statement summarizing the individual's research focus, major contributions, relevant expertise, and relevance to the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe current research focus, significant achievements, areas of expertise, mentoring/training experience, and why the investigator is well suited to contribute to the proposed project (examples shown in the biosketch personal statements for the applicants).

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Positions and Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: A chronological listing of positions/occupations (with start/end dates), field, institution/company, and supervisors/employers, plus academic and professional honors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide dates (mm/yy), activity/occupation, field, institution/company, and any notable honors or awards; format as a clear table or list to allow quick reviewer appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Contributions to Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbered narrative statements of major scientific contributions, each accompanied by a brief explanation and representative publications (with PMCID/PMID where available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each major contribution provide a succinct description (what was discovered or developed, its significance), followed by representative publications and citation details; can include descriptions of methods/techniques developed and invited lectures as supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Additional Information: Research Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Listing of ongoing and completed research support relevant to the person, including grant numbers, titles, funding agency, project periods, and role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include current/ongoing support (grant number, e.g., F32 AG 053023; project title; funding agency; project period dates) and clarify role on the grant; this documents available resources and potential overlap of effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: RESEARCH & RELATED Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) — required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Form fields to be completed for each senior/key person: name, eRA Commons user name (credential), position title, organization name, department/division, address components, phone, e-mail, credential, project role, degree type/year, and file attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all required fields (marked with *). Provide Project Role (e.g., PD/PI), attach Biographical Sketch and Current & Pending Support files, and include tracking/funding opportunity numbers as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach required files
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach Biographical Sketch and Current & Pending Support for each senior/key person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure file names are provided (examples: Applicant_Biosketch_R1.pdf, Current_and_Pending_Support_R1.pdf) and that attachments correspond to the person's profile; include tracking numbers and Funding Opportunity Number where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — laboratory space and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe laboratory space (square footage, benches/desks, instrument rooms, microscope rooms, cold room), office space, and the collaborative environment (neighboring labs, shared facilities, machine and electronic shops, supply rooms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete details (e.g., '3320 sq. ft. of renovated lab space, benches and desks for 21 scientists, 3 instrument rooms, 3 microscope rooms, and 1 cold room'), name neighboring labs and shared resources, and indicate willingness to share state-of-the-art facilities relevant to the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — equipment, cores, and services
rubrics_metrics.description: List owned or accessible equipment and core facilities (incubators, -80°C freezers, ultracentrifuge, PCR machines, microscopy systems, COPAS Biosort, confocal/light-sheet microscopes, proteomics/mass spec and genomics sequencing labs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give specifics about capabilities and availability (e.g., numbers and models of microscopes, presence of a Genomics Sequencing Laboratory for Illumina platforms, access to Proteomics/Mass Spectrometry Laboratory) and assert that these systems 'offer all the capabilities required for the proposed experiments.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — media, buffers, and core prep facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe shared media and buffer preparation facilities and equipment (e.g., media center size, mediaclaves for automated plate pouring, autoclaves, reagent prep infrastructure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide facility location relative to lab (e.g., '500 sq. ft. media center housed at Koshland Hall next door'), list key devices (e.g., two thirty liter mediaclaves), and state that necessary equipment for reagent preparation is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — computing resources and software
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe computing hardware, servers, network infrastructure, storage capacity, and licensed software available to personnel (workstations, Linux servers, CPU cores, RAM, TB storage, network bandwidth, VPN, PRISM, MATLAB, image processing and sequencing analysis tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide performance details (e.g., 'Linux workstations have 16 to 32 CPU cores and 64 to 128 GB of RAM', 'file servers host a total of 173 TB and read at 1.5 GB/sec'), state network topology and bandwidth (20 Gigabit/sec intranet for instruments, Gigabit/sec internal network), list software licenses (PRISM, MATLAB, bowtie2, SAMtools, deepTools, macs2, bedtools, tophat, cufflinks), and note remote access options (VPN).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — imaging resources and capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail imaging instrumentation and software (microscope models, time-lapse and automated microscopy, licenses for deconvolution software, access to Molecular Imaging Center resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List owned instruments and access (e.g., Zeiss AxioObserver.Z1 with apotome, Leica SP8 confocal, diSPIM light-sheet, PerkinElmer spinning disk confocal, SIM/STORM-capable systems), note specialized hardware (COPAS Biosort) and software (Huygens Deconvolution), and state that together the systems support the proposed experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource applicability statements (Clinical / Animal / Computer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate applicability of clinical and animal resources and provide details for computer resources: e.g., 'Clinical: Not Applicable.' 'Animal: N/A.' 'Computer: Every member...equipped with his/her own Macintosh computer or PC...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state when clinical and animal resources are not applicable to the project. For computing, describe per-person computers, shared workstations, VPN access, server/file-sharing, and institutional access to journals and databases.
